F_s and g_s have strictly positive second derivatives and h strictly negative second derivative across every admissible occupancy. Each unbalanced pair transfer lowers J strictly, proving all and only balanced conditional optima; comparison of two explicit costs exhausts all m-subsets. Three-leader thresholds arise by exact rational subtraction. Symbolic and exact principal-inverse replay corroborates the critical identities; infinite proof is analytical.

value.rationale: For a motivated family of modular hub-and-clique consensus networks, choosing m noise-free leaders involves exponentially many vertex subsets. The theorem determines every exact global optimizer from two closed rational expressions for any m, including multiplicities and nontrivial sharp three-leader changes in hub selection. Strict balancing simultaneously optimizes multiple nonlinearly competing Schur terms; this is a structural all-budget result rather than an isolated small-instance computation.
